newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi firm wins deal to run grain port terminal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi firm wins deal to run grain port terminal.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has chosen a local firm to run a terminal handling imports of bulk wheat at its Red Sea port of Jeddah, Saudi officials said on Saturday.

The move is part of a plan to let the private sector take over operation, maintenance and management of docks and equipment used by Saudi Arabia's ports authority, SEAPA. All operations would be on a commercial basis.
The officials said the Jeddah-based AJWA-R.M.T.I, a private enterprise that produces rice, was chosen over four other firms, the officials said. A final deal will be signed soon.
SEAPA said last month it had shortlisted 43 firms to bid for six projects under a scheme to upgrade ports and boost handling capability.
AJWA officials were not available for comment. But the Saudi business daily al-Eqtisadiah said on Saturday AJWA would buy machinery to handle five million tonnes of wheat a year.

Its terminal would meet the needs of all bulk wheat importers and exporters at a handling cost of eight riyals ($2) per tonne. AJWA would also package grain for re-export to neighbouring states and offer vocational training for Saudis to replace expatriate workers.
Under the gradual privatisation plan, SEAPA would retain its supervisory role over the ports on the Red Sea and Gulf coasts and ensure there were no rises in handling fees.

The six projects include cargo terminals at the eastern ports of Damman and Jubail, a roll-on roll-off (RORO) goods terminal at Jeddah and the management of King Fahd ship repair complex, the officials said. Projects have a leasing period of 10 years.

Total turnover at the kingdom's six main commercial and two industrial ports reached 87 million tonnes in 1996 compared with 80 million tonnes in 1995, official figures say. Jeddah handles nearly one million containers a year, making it the kingdom's busiest port.
